verdicts.claim: A checkpoint moves the transactions in the WAL file back into the main database file. SQLite runs one automatically when a COMMIT leaves
verdicts.evidence: wal.html 3.1: 'automatically checkpoint whenever a COMMIT occurs that causes the WAL file to be 1000 pages or more in size, or when the last database connection on a database file closes'; sec 6 'about 1000 pages (and is thus about 4MB'; SQLITE_DEFAULT_WAL_AUTOCHECKPOINT named in 2.1

verdicts.claim: PASSIVE mode copies as many frames as it can without waiting for readers or writers. It never calls the busy handler... FULL... RESTART... TRUNCATE
verdicts.evidence: wal_checkpoint_v2 page defines all four modes as stated, incl. 'truncates the log file to zero bytes just prior to a successful return'

verdicts.claim: A checkpoint must stop at the first WAL frame that is newer than the end mark of any current reader. It records its progress in the wal-index
verdicts.evidence: wal.html 2.2: 'must stop when it reaches a page in the WAL that is past the end mark of any current reader... remembers (in the wal-index) how far it got'; 'a long-running read transaction can prevent a checkpointer from making progress'

verdicts.claim: A normal checkpoint does not shrink the WAL file... journal_size_limit setting (default -1, meaning no limit; 0 means always truncate
verdicts.evidence: pragma.html: 'The default journal size limit is -1 (no limit)'; 'set the journal_size_limit to zero' to always truncate; 'must be set separately for each attached database'; wal.html 6: overwrite faster than append

verdicts.claim: PRAGMA wal_autocheckpoint=N, or the sqlite3_wal_autocheckpoint() C function, sets the auto-checkpoint threshold in pages. Setting N to zero
verdicts.evidence: pragma.html: 'Setting the auto-checkpoint size to zero or a negative value turns auto-checkpointing off... All automatic checkpoints are PASSIVE'

verdicts.claim: NOOP mode copies no frames. Its only use is to read the WAL size (*pnLog) and the number of frames already checkpointed (*pnCkpt)
verdicts.evidence: v2 page: 'only reason to invoke a NOOP checkpoint is to access the values returned... upon successful completion of an SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_TRUNCATE... both *pnLog and *pnCkpt will be set to zero'

verdicts.claim: PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(MODE) returns one row with three columns. The first is busy: 0 means SQLITE_OK, and 1 means a FULL, RESTART or
verdicts.evidence: pragma.html: 'returns a single row with three integer columns... second and third column are -1 if there is no write-ahead log'; no-arg form 'equivalent to calling the sqlite3_wal_checkpoint()' (= PASSIVE). Minor: source words col 2 as 'modified pages written to the WAL'

verdicts.claim: Litestream keeps a long-running read transaction open so that no other process can checkpoint and restart the WAL. Litestream then
verdicts.evidence: how-it-works: 'starts a long-running read transaction to prevent any other process from checkpointing and restarting the WAL file... continually reads new WAL pages and manually calls out to SQLite to perform checkpoints'

verdicts.claim: Checkpoint starvation: if there is always at least one overlapping reader, no checkpoint completes and the WAL file grows without bound
verdicts.evidence: wal.html 6: 'always at least one active reader, then no checkpoints will be able to complete... "reader gaps"... SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_RESTART or SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_TRUNCATE... readers might block'

verdicts.claim: Disabling auto-checkpoint without running checkpoints yourself lets the WAL grow without limit. A large WAL also slows reads
verdicts.evidence: wal.html 6 'nothing to prevent the WAL file from growing excessively'; 2.3 'read performance deteriorates as the WAL file grows'; read/write checkpoint-frequency tradeoff stated

verdicts.claim: Every checkpoint takes an exclusive checkpoint lock. If another connection is already checkpointing, the call returns SQLITE_BUSY at once
verdicts.evidence: v2 page: 'All calls obtain an exclusive "checkpoint" lock... SQLITE_BUSY is returned. Even if there is a busy-handler configured, it will not be invoked'; busy-handler 0 → 'proceeds... same way as SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_PASSIVE... SQLITE_BUSY is returned'. 'TRUNCATE does not shrink' is inference from 'just prior to a successful return'

verdicts.claim: Disagreement: SQLite docs present RESTART/TRUNCATE as the remedy for starvation; Litestream warns blocking TRUNCATE stalls writes
verdicts.evidence: Litestream: 'TRUNCATE checkpoints will block writes until all read transactions complete'; 'Applications with long-lived read transactions: Set truncate-page-n: 0'

verdicts.claim: Disagreement: sqlite3_wal_checkpoint_v2 page says RESTART 'does not impede readers'; wal.html says 'readers might block while the checkpoint
verdicts.evidence: Both quoted phrases appear verbatim in the respective pages

verdicts.claim: Open: current official guide says min-checkpoint-page-count is 1000 pages (about 4 MB) and the emergency threshold is about 500 MB
verdicts.evidence: Guide: 'min-checkpoint-page-count: 1000 # Default : ~4MB'; 'truncate-page-n: 121359 # Default : ~500MB'. The 10 MB snippet claim itself is uncited and was not checked
